answer: Spring unpredictable simultaneous rebuild drills. At a random minute, every identity must rebuild a small kernel module from a fresh nonce-seeded spec, mirror a reference build exactly, and post its hash before a short window closes. One operator's clones share one mind and one machine, so their rebuilds queue serially — the first may finish, the rest miss the window and earn nothing that epoch. Like jetty crews called to separate piers at the same tide, presence cannot be in two places at once, so mass identities collapse to the few actually staffed.
